method: SEED, not a ceiling, since specs/022 L4b (2026-09-06). These p95 values PRE-FILL each tag's running window in AppendBudget; the bar is the tag's own recent rate once real ticks have pushed the seed out, because the quantity is NOT stationary -- measured over 1200 ticks, per-tick 0x07 bytes climb 52,763 -> 77,998 B monotonically, carried by whole frames that grow with the brain. A stale seed now costs 3 floods instead of alarming forever. Other consumer: immortal_retention.budget_coverage(), the census of which immortal tags have ever been measured. ORIGINAL METHOD, kept because it is what these numbers are: BinLog.append+extend wrap over make_brain(seed=0) x120 ticks, NORD_HOME scratch; p95 over nonzero per-tick byte sums. Re-measured at T012 post-cutover: growth lands under 0x08 (chain deltas, 0 legacy ticks measured); 0x03's ceiling is CARRIED from the T010-i measurement, not re-measured -- the legacy tag is closed to npz writes since T010-ii, so any 0x03 flood is a regression the budget should still catch. 0x0A added post-T032 (2026-08-21), same instrument: 61 nonzero of 120 ticks (sleep ticks emit no coalitions -- honest zeros excluded per the method), p95 434 B, max 435, mean 381.2; the live daemon's first hour under T031 wrote 15,080 records, consistent with this per-tick rate at daemon cadence
